subject: Apparent bug in legend display when size is customized with scale_size()

messages.author: 363861a949524eb3
messages.subject: Apparent bug in legend display when size is customized with scale_size()
parts:
Hi,

The legend panel appears broken when one is specifying custom breaks
for the size attribute while there is a somewhat large range of
continuous values to be represented as the size. The points in the
legend panel are all of small size.

Example:

# test data
dataf <- data.frame(x=c(3, 6, 10, 20, 300, 10E3))
# plot
ggplot(dataf) +
geom_point(aes(x=x, y=x, size=x)) +
scale_size_continuous(breaks=c(0,3,6,10))



L.

messages.subject: Re: Apparent bug in legend display when size is customized with scale_size()
parts:
If you specify a limit, you get the sizes that you want in the legend, but it removes points (which I assume you don't want).

#test data

dataf <- data.frame(x=c(3, 6, 10, 20, 300, 10E3))
# plot
ggplot(dataf) +
 geom_point(aes(x=x, y=x, size=x)) +

scale_size_continuous(limit = c(0,10), breaks=c(0,3,6,10))

If you want anything bigger than 10 to be the same size as 10 you'd probably be better off using cut() to specify levels of a factor and then plot that using scale_size_manual(). Although, I think plotting in such a way would probably be misleading. 

You could also try using a log transformation of the scale since your numbers are so massively different. 

Brandon

messages.subject: Re: Apparent bug in legend display when size is customized with scale_size()
parts:
In this case, they are there, but overplotted. 

dataf$a<-cut(dataf$x, breaks=c(0,3,6,10,+Inf))

ggplot(dataf)+
  geom_point(aes(x=x, y=x, 
                 size=a), alpha=0.3)

Plot attached. Notice the more intense black in the bottom dot. 

B
